subject: filecabinet
label: filecabinet.mdl, in the place of the game's models/filecabinet.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_gauss.mdl, models/w_oxygen.mdl, models/w_suit.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, D, D, B where the asset was C, A, D, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Every view in sides.png has the outline of a plain rectangular filing cabinet: flat sides, a flat top, a slightly lighter rim around the edges, and no part sticking out or missing. The front-left and front-right views match the front and right views in height and depth.

M2.reason: The measured size is 29 x 23 x 62 against the brief's 62 tall, 29 deep and 23 wide, so sizeOff is 0 and each dimension is within 15%.

M3.reason: The brief's parts are three drawers, three handles, a label holder and the box. All three drawers are present, stacked in the same places, with seams between them in the front views. All three handles are present as dark bars on each drawer front, and they read clearly in the lineup at game size. The small label holder is a painted gold card on the top drawer, which counts as there because it reads at size. The brief names no round part, claws, teeth, rivets or tabs, so there is no facet count to check. Nothing is missing.

M4.reason: The cabinet is grey metal with dark painted handles and a lighter rim, which matches a grey steel cabinet. The top reads as brushed metal. The sides are mottled, a little like stone, but at game size that reads as the grimy steel the brief asks for, so I judged the material as right. No measure was given for this item; the score is by eye.

M5.reason: The brief asks for a bit of grime. The side panels carry darker mottling and a few dark streaks, and the drawer seams, the handles and the gold label are all in their places at a sharpness that suits the game. The fine detail is soft but in the same band as Half-Life's own metal props.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up. In the four readings the judges picked the asset's own slot twice (two of four) and missed twice, which does not reach the three catches that would lower M6. The asset sits in lineup.png beside Valve's props at the same scale and does not stand out as off.

M7.reason: The drawers and the label face the front, the cabinet stands upright, and it sits on its base as a filing cabinet does. The front view and the three drawers agree on which face is the front.

M8.reason: The reported check errors list is empty, so SMAK's GoldSrc check passes. 60 triangles is well under twice the median of 238 for Half-Life's props of its kind and size. The only open face is the underside, which is dark in the BELOW view. A player standing on the floor cannot see it, so it is not a visible opening. Nothing floats or is inside out.
